name: Mantis Manta
anatomy: Paired upright serrated raptorial forelegs above a broad webbed manta planform, a bare needle spine, and thin trailing jelly tendrils.

name: Lacewing Medusa
anatomy: A domed bell over a lacewing thorax with four long translucent wings and loose, hair-thin hanging tentacles.

name: Sawtail Skate
anatomy: Long pointed snout, swept triangular skeletal fins, and a single exaggerated serrated tail.

name: Ribcage Medusa
anatomy: Split beetle carapace revealing exposed rib arches, small antennae and free-hanging fine tentacles.

name: Skeletal Moth Ray
anatomy: Fenestrated broad wing membranes, feathered moth antennae, and tapering tendrils that drift off-axis.

name: Stiltback
anatomy: A spiked horseshoe carapace with a sharp keel, central feelers and six delicate articulated stilt legs.

name: Wasp Bell
anatomy: A translucent medusa dome over a wasp thorax, thin veined flight wings, and pendulous feelers.

name: Bone Kite
anatomy: Sharp triangular bone kite fins, arthropod jaws and a rigid piercing tail.

name: Centipede Ray
anatomy: An S-shaped segmented centipede spine with ray sails by the head, needle ribs, and long flexible filament fringe.

name: Umbrella Crab
anatomy: Angular segmented spider crab with pinching claws under a floating umbrella bell and dangling tentacles.

name: Antler Ray
anatomy: A branching pair of prominent antlers above broad, open webbed ray fins with fine trailing tentacles.

name: Dragonfly Siphonophore
anatomy: Four gossamer veined wings lead a chain of translucent medusae with free-flowing threadlike appendages.

name: Rib Fan
anatomy: Radial stiff ribs bow upward into an inverted fan above long limp tentacles and a narrow central spine.

name: Lantern Pupa
anatomy: Tall segmented pupa enclosed in a translucent skeletal lantern, with looping tentacles and narrow tips.

name: Strider Ray
anatomy: Narrow ray wings and a tiny thorax with four very long bent needle legs and fine central tendrils.

name: Trilobite Bell
anatomy: A low medusa dome with swept-back exposed trilobite ribs and thin streaming jelly tentacles.

name: Scorpion Ray
anatomy: Crescent wings tipped in long forward hooks and a segmented tail curled around a pointed stinger.

name: Feather Isopod
anatomy: Overlapping plates under a pair of feathered antennae with needle legs and a soft filament tail.

name: Flea Jelly
anatomy: C-shaped segmented carapace with articulated flea legs above a trailing fringe of gelatinous filaments.

name: Needle Crown
anatomy: Broad open ring of bone with upward needle spines and a full curtain of hairlike tentacles.

name: Prism Thorn
anatomy: A narrow diamond ray with a tall central prism of perforated bone and elegantly forked outer wing tips. Four curved sensory barbels hang below its keel.

name: Chandelier Bell
anatomy: Three small nested scalloped bells aligned vertically on one body, progressively smaller beneath the upper dome, with long knotted threads and wishbone-shaped radial supports.

name: Gauntlet Crawler
anatomy: A squat plated arthropod seen dorsally, featuring massive asymmetrical gauntlet claws, tiny secondary pincers, and long needle legs extending behind it.

name: Suture Ribbon
anatomy: A narrow translucent ribbon swimmer folded in a broad descending zigzag, with bands of stitched vertebral joints, two filament crests, and a long split tail.

name: Forkglass Ray
anatomy: An arrowhead ray with glassy perforated membranes and a deeply forked center, holding a slender tuning-fork tail between two finely serrated hind fins.

name: Widow Lantern
anatomy: A long pear-shaped bell with a pointed cap, a dense dark hourglass core visible through the membrane, and eight unequal whip tentacles curling toward the center.

name: Halo Scarab
anatomy: A beetle-shaped abyssal crustacean encircled by two split curved horns forming a broken halo, with ridged black wing covers, a bony thorax, and delicate six-legged spread.

name: Spool Eel
anatomy: A wiry eel-like alien coiled into two spacious loop turns with its needle-jawed head lifted outward, fin-spines piercing along the outside, and a trailing fan of threads.

name: Needle Harp
anatomy: A broad rectangular ray silhouette with concave edges, twin parallel spine rails, thin long filaments like harp strings between ragged side fins, and a spined whip tail.

name: Ruffle Umbel
anatomy: A low wide fan-shaped medusa viewed in three-quarter profile with overlapping ruffled lobes, curled bony radial vanes, and shimmering hair-fine tentacles swept off toward one corner.

name: Cathedral Louse
anatomy: A flattened chitin crawler tapering into a ribbed tail, with three buttresslike dorsal arches, braided bifurcating antennae, and thin legs with pointed metal-dark joints.

name: Hourglass Siphon
anatomy: A vertical hourglass-shaped siphonophore with two slender colonies of translucent lobes joined by a tight skeletal waist, each ending in long skeins of filament.

name: Broadfork Skate
anatomy: A low, broad skate with two unequal crescent wing lobes, clubbed bone struts, and a double-pronged tapering spine extending diagonally across the format.

name: Veil Bishop
anatomy: A tall mitre-shaped jellyfish with open, clean bell paneling and asymmetrical veils hanging like torn membranes, bordered by delicate barbs and scattered fine tentacles.

name: Lockjaw Shrimp
anatomy: A curved mantis-shrimp silhouette in clean profile with two linked folding claw blades, a black ventral spine, skeletal keel plates, and paired antennae longer than its body.

name: Hemline Wraith
anatomy: A streamer creature with wide overlapping translucent fin folds twisting down one margin, tiny exposed vertebrae down the opposing edge, and long hairline threads following the twist.

name: Halberd Ray
anatomy: A ray built around a long hooked spearhead snout offset above swept delta wings, with asymmetrical shoulder blades, bone-veined membranes, and hanging tentacles from the wingtips.

name: Lattice Urn
anatomy: A jelly shaped like an open urn with a crown of bone loops at the neck, narrow transparent sides, and thread tentacles curling outward from an inverted lower funnel.

name: Splinter Flea
anatomy: A laterally viewed delicate flea with a compressed, sharply arched abdomen, open triangular ribs, folded spring-loaded rear legs, and a pair of long whisker spines curling forward.

name: Slitfin Leech
anatomy: A sinuous flattened leech with a slit-shaped mouth, translucid fins cut into large leaflike paired petals, and fine whiplike appendages on a long reverse curl.

name: Wheel Mantle
anatomy: A round manta with an incomplete outer halo of curved chitin rays and a tiny skull-like center, showing radial bone ribs, a loose ring of thin spines, and a split flowing tail.

name: Incense Bell
anatomy: A tiny flat cap bell with clusters of very long undulating, braided tendrils flowing in one broad arcing mass, and short jagged whitebone prongs caging the cap.

name: Grave Cicada
anatomy: A sharp-bodied cicada with veined folding pectoral fins held close to exposed rib plates, enormous upright hooked tibiae, and an odd cluster of sensory rods on top.

name: Comb Serpent
anatomy: A double-curved sea serpent with closely spaced paddle-like comb plates along the inside of its S curve, a tiny split beak, and fine translucent scalloped fins along the outer turns.

name: Nacre Scythe
anatomy: A ray with deeply scalloped forward-hooking crescent wings, pitted ribs and a slender dangling septum of cartilage, with three long thread tails reaching in separate arcs.

name: Shuttle Ghost
anatomy: A horizontal spindle-shaped jelly with a transparent capsule of fine longitudinal ribs, two long frilled oral arms sweeping backward, and a filament fringe at each tapered end.

name: Stitch Crab
anatomy: A squat hexagonal shoreless crab covered with pierced bone sutures, split thin asymmetrical stalking legs, a prominent pair of swept fork pincers, and dangling barbed mouth feelers.

name: Sicklefin
anatomy: A sharply asymmetric skate with one high crescent fin and one truncated hook, ribbed membrane, a split skull at the nose, and a thin sabre-like tail that curves across the body axis.

name: Thimble Lantern
anatomy: A narrow thimble-shaped bell with vertical capsule windows, a single suspended pearlescent-looking seed inside the cup, and sparse threadlike tentacles beaded at uneven heights.

name: Harrow Mite
anatomy: A low diamond body of dovetailed bone plates, a comb of backward head spines, and four pairs of hooked grazing legs with fine trailing bristles.

name: Vertebral Pennant
anatomy: A vertical flowing pennant of porous bone vertebrae, open alternating long ventral and short dorsal fins, and a set of loose side tendrils that continue the S-curve.

name: Keyhole Skate
anatomy: Broad arched fins curl inward over a circular keyhole-shaped opening in the middle of the body, supported by fine rib struts. Two whip tails trail widely apart.

name: Parasail Bloom
anatomy: A wide domed membrane with five swept lobes, a small keel hanging loose from the center under the bell, and a few cablelike horn-tipped tentacles pulled out diagonally.

name: Rakeback Treader
anatomy: A long armored oval with seven rows of rake-like dorsal needles and six slender hinged legs stepping outward. An angular pair of jaw tines project from its head.

name: Zipper Leech
anatomy: An undulating flattened creature with two offset rows of interlocking tiny hooked vertebrae and a dark seam along the center. Spindly fins protrude in pairs, ending in threadlike feelers.

name: Lace Delta
anatomy: A pronounced triangular silhouette with a needle snout, thin trailing membranes divided into a triangular mesh, long elbow spines and three fine tails fanning from a single bony socket.

name: Chime Cluster
anatomy: One colonial jelly with three small linked hanging bells around a central trunk, like asymmetric chimes. Distinct hairline tentacles spill from the lowest mouths, and a filigree tendon joins all bells.

name: Pincer Spindle
anatomy: A vertically suspended spindle-bodied animal in dorsal view, with one pair of fine pincer forelimbs far above the head, a narrow waist enclosed by clear shell, and tapered hind legs hinged beneath.

name: Whiplace Eel
anatomy: A clean sinuous knot of narrow vertebrae in diagonal profile, with fringe-like one-sided spines and almost invisible threads spreading across the gaps. A long tapering snout leads the curve.

name: Horizon Ray
anatomy: An extremely flat wingspan held nearly horizontal, with scale-like open channels in each fin. The broad body breaks into a narrow central lance underneath and two fine streamer fins.

name: Mourning Hood
anatomy: A bell like an inverted hood in three-quarter view, with its lip descending at the left and opening onto a thin skeletal faceplate. A translucent layered veil drapes to one side into tentacles.

name: Needle Cicada
anatomy: A cicada-like bony thorax with tightly folded narrow wings as long as the body, two bulging chitin sockets, and slim front legs ending in needle hooks against the ivory.

name: Twin Strand
anatomy: A single creature with a Y-shaped central cartilage column dividing halfway down into two streams of tapering vertebrae. A fine drawn web of membranes spans between the branches, with free tentacle tips beyond them.

name: Lantern Kite
anatomy: A diamond ray with one translucent lanternlike window at each shoulder, segmented longfin spars, a tapered faceplate and four thin whiplashes flowing behind the wing roots.

name: Lobed Chalice
anatomy: An upright cup-shaped gelatinous crown with eight uneven petal lobes and strainers of curved ribs, narrowing into a long segmented stem and finishing in thread-fine roots.

name: Stitch Mantis
anatomy: A head-down acrobatic swimmer with ribbed raptorial arms crossing underneath a chitin thorax, two small lace-cut swimming fins, and a segmented abdomen cinched with stitchlike bone bridges.

name: Fin Suture
anatomy: A ribbon creature drifting in a broad U, composed of skin-thin paired fin panels edged in dark lines, articulated at an exposed spiny backbone, with threads trailing from each tip.

name: Cowl Skate
anatomy: A compact rounded ray with two inward-rolled fins folding like a cowl around a small central skeletal head. The back unfolds as a thin triangular tail with filaments curving from its tip.

name: Glass Inkwell
anatomy: An angular glass-bottle-shaped medusa, the squashy square shoulder supported by graceful sweeping ribs and a tubular downward-facing mouth. Fine tentacles descend from four distinct anchors.

name: Ridgeback Flea
anatomy: A squat tightly curled swimmer in side profile, with two overlapping ridges above ringed armor, long folded spring legs and tiny tufted antennae. Stinging threads trail from the cap of the tail.

name: Crozier Worm
anatomy: A thin segmented animal curled downward like a crozier, with raised hooked spines along the back and a delicate zigzag frill running from head to tail. Floating tentacle strands continue the curl below.

name: Combwing Skate
anatomy: Flat scalloped wings on either side of a long exposed spine, each fin divided into delicate comb projections. The inner fin carries a sparse transparent sheet and the terminus of the spine forks into two tendrils.

name: Pearl Cage
anatomy: A round open skeletal cage of long narrow tapered ribs encircles a pale ovoid inner organ. Threads drip from the uneven lower rim while three sharp crest spines extend up from the dome.

name: Barbed Oarling
anatomy: An oval, seven-segment chitin body with paired broad bone oars near the front, a serrated crown and several dainty hind legs spun out into spines. A loose bundle of hairlike tentacles drifts back between two tail flukes.

name: Suture Sail
anatomy: very wide triangular fins joined by visible stitchlike bone bridges, a short twin-pronged tail and one broad veiled central keel

name: Opal Thimble
anatomy: compact perforated thimble-shaped bell with a crown of nine small needle spines, three thicker ribbon tentacles and hair-fine secondary threads

name: Tripod Mite
anatomy: three distinctly articulated long bowed legs around a tiny round shell and a short sensory tendril behind each knee

name: Notch Eel
anatomy: long asymmetric S-curved ribbon with alternately notched bone plates, two fanlike rib sails near the pointed face and sparse thin trailing barbs

name: Prism Skate
anatomy: near-diamond ray wings divided into pane-like membranes, narrow beaked skull, paired slender rear forks and long hanging wingtip tassels

name: Gnomon Medusa
anatomy: shallow tilted jelly bell punctured by a single gnomon-like dorsal spine, a thick spiral oral arm and a skirt of very thin filaments

name: Latch Beetle
anatomy: spindle-shaped segmented beetle built around two open hooked mandibles that close like a latch, six thin bent legs and downward feelers

name: Spiral Rattle
anatomy: steep corkscrew body with repeated loose vertebral hoops, dorsal quill spines and two whisker fans framing a narrow bony head

name: Harp Skate
anatomy: left and right sickle-shaped ray wings linked by taut strings of tissue to a deep central chest keel, with a needle tail and paired soft streamers

name: Hourglass Bell
anatomy: two lobes meeting at a pinched waist, an outer rib cage arcing around the upper bell, loose threads streaming from the lower lobe

name: Railhopper
anatomy: tiny narrow carapace and two dramatically lengthened hinged jumping legs, backed by four small forelimbs and paired whiplike antennae

name: Thorn Chain
anatomy: an undulating string of open diamond vertebrae interleaved with thorn spines, converging into three strands of fine tail tendrils

name: Razor Crown Ray
anatomy: crescent swept-forward ray fins bearing sharp comb projections, a crown of short forehead fangs, and a long flowing tubular tail

name: Glass Basket Jelly
anatomy: round open basket of curved ivory ribs under a translucent bell, four trailing looped ribbons and many smaller fine tentacles

name: Bishop Crab
anatomy: a tall spired shell in the shape of a pointed arch, two chunky hinged claws, six long delicate segmented legs, and short central feelers

name: Needle Rosary
anatomy: a descending curve of linked beadlike vertebrae pierced by long transverse needle spines, translucent tail frill almost as long as the body

name: Sicklefin Ray
anatomy: oar-shaped fin on one side and a short recurved sickle membrane on the other, chiseled spine and one razor-thin looping tail

name: Lily Bell
anatomy: a split petal bell with scalloped bony rims, four pronounced trailing oral arms and several fine threads lifted up by the current

name: Tripwire Isopod
anatomy: flattened shield of long overlapping armor plates, eight skeletal articulated leg pairs and two enormous trailing antennae that bend like wire

name: Oculus Siphon
anatomy: a curving chain of translucent annular chambers decreasing toward the tail, narrow bony ribs in the voids and a forked flexible filament finish

name: Cowl Manta
anatomy: a high armored hood over a delicate jaw, butterflylike swept wings broken into three membrane lobes per side, long soft trailing tassels

name: Porcelain Bell
anatomy: small opaque fluted dome with decorative fracturelike radial ridges, a segmented center spindle, and several loose curling hair-thin tentacles

name: Mourning Cicada
anatomy: blade-shaped insect torso, two large intricately veined wings, paired segmented forelegs that curve around the head and loose tail filaments

name: Loom Cestus
anatomy: a wide transparent, doubly scalloped ribbon held by two axial bone rails and repeated diagonal struts, tapering to a loose whip

name: Halo Manta
anatomy: broad webbed disc with edge gaps and skeletal spokes, paired head forks framing one dark center opening, and two long tetherlike tentacles

name: Cathedral Medusa
anatomy: immense sharply peaked bell with tiers of gothic arch ribs and bony pinnacles, scores of hair-thin tentacles, central twisting oral spires
